body.text: A proposal, and I will put it to you before I put it to anybody else.

I know of a very wise botanist much taken with the cultivation of sugar cane in the colonies. He is presently in Bristol, being disagreed with. I could see him equipped with supplies and a labour force, and he will found a settlement in country suited to the purpose.

It will not walk there. The Crown will carry it — ships, guards, a surgeon, the whole business — and it will be five months before you see it. Nothing will happen to it on the way, which is what you are paying for.
What it arrives as depends entirely on what you are willing to put behind it. I have set out three answers below and I will not pretend to be neutral between them.
{param:amount} for the handsome version. Less for less. I would take the least of them over nothing, but I would think less of the arrangement.

tone.text: Dr Meakin — on your botanist I am {choice}.

options.label: equip it handsomely
options.text: Equip it properly. If we are doing this we are not doing it by halves.

options.label: equip it adequately
options.text: Enough to stand it up, and no more. They may earn the rest.

options.label: send them with what you can spare
options.text: Send them. I cannot pretend to furnish them, and I will not pretend it is generous.

options.label: argue him out of it
options.text: I would rather you did not. We have towns enough that cannot feed themselves without adding another.

closing.text: I am, sir, your obedient servant,
